title: Minimum Number of Platforms
hints: the answer is the maximum number of trains simultaneously at the station at any instant - how could you find that peak without checking every instant individually?
sort the arrival times and the departure times separately, each in ascending order
walk both sorted lists together: whenever the next event chronologically is an arrival, a platform is now needed; whenever it's a departure, a platform is freed

track a running count of platforms in use, updating a maximum as you go - when arrival[i] <= departure[j], that's a new arrival needing a platform before that next departure frees one, so increment; otherwise a departure happens first, so decrement

why does sorting the two arrays independently still give the correct answer, even though it destroys the pairing between a train's own arrival and departure? because the count of platforms in use at any moment only depends on how many arrivals-so-far exceed departures-so-far, not on which specific train is on which platform
commonMistakes: treating an arrival and departure at the exact same time as overlapping (they should not require an extra platform, since the departing train frees its platform first)
sorting the two arrays as pairs (keeping arrival[i] linked to departure[i]) instead of sorting each array independently, which breaks the two-pointer sweep
computing only the count of trains active at the very first or last event instead of tracking the running maximum across the whole sweep

content.problemStatement:
A train station has trains arriving and departing throughout the day. You're given `arrival`, where `arrival[i]` is the arrival time of the i-th train, and `departure`, where `departure[i]` is its departure time. A train occupies the same platform the whole time it's at the station, and a platform becomes free the moment a train departs.

**Return the minimum number of platforms needed so that no two trains present at the station at the same time ever need the same platform.**
notes: all trains overlap at the same instant (needs a platform per train)
no trains overlap at all (needs only 1 platform)
a train's departure exactly equals another's arrival (does not count as an overlap)
